cands.name: Jessie Barcala

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Retired after 25 years of government service. Former U.S. Air Force Explosive Ordnance Disposal technician with deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan, then a Transportation Security Specialist in Huntsville. Owns a security consultation and training business. Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 5 in 2026. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from the Sway voting groups Be. A. Menace (Kate for the People), Tabitha's List (Tabitha Isner), and Unburdening The Ballot (Tevin Davis). These are voter-guide recommendations, not organizational endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Jessie Barcala was born. His military, TSA and FBI career, his business and his Alabama upbringing come only from his own campaign site, with no independent confirmation. He has held no public office, so there is no voting or legislative record. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. His campaign site's issue pages give only brief summaries on affordability, housing, infrastructure, veterans' services, healthcare and transparency. We found no specific stated positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership limits, immigration, guns, abortion, or school choice. His housing summary mentions responsible development that preserves community character, but gives no specific policy. No news coverage or controversies turned up.

cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 5 since February 2016. Former state director of the Farm Service Agency and crop insurance contractor. Served on the Athens City Council from 1993 to 2005. Holds B.A. and M.A. degrees from Auburn University.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Danny Crawford was born or raised, or when he moved to Alabama. We found no stated positions or documented actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2022 or 2026, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for 2026. The list of bills he sponsored did not load on the page we read, so we left it out. His specific roles at the Farm Service Agency and dates there are not given.
